decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach to the leftmost camera; assign cameras to white, vehicles to blue, watches to red. Initial depth and fingertip offset remain approximate.
Bring left gripper toward the left camera with a downward-facing approach, keeping the elbow-up branch and gripper open.
Use wrist view to correct left and back while descending toward the camera; keep orientation fixed for alignment.
Center the camera between the left fingers, close, and make a short test lift to verify retention visually.
Lift the visually retained camera clear of the table and carry toward the white basket, keeping the left gripper closed.
Lower and release the first camera inside white, then clear its rim. Begin the right arm's elbow-up approach to the rightmost watch.
Move left above the next camera while right aligns over the rear watch; maintain height until both wrist views confirm alignment.
Descend in small increments with minor lateral corrections toward the second camera and rear watch. Both grippers stay open until alignment is clearer.
Wrist views show both targets forward of the pinch line; retract toward the robot while completing the gentle descent.
Correct the observed wrist-image motion: advance both open grippers toward their targets at constant height, rather than retracting farther.
Close on the centered camera and watch, then make a short vertical test lift. Check RGB retention before transporting.
Retention is uncertain: targets stayed near the table and fingers closed together. Reopen and lower for a deeper grasp; offset right toward the watch housing.
Adjust the deeper pinch to the shifted camera and watch, close, and test-lift a small amount before committing to transport.
Both objects appear seated between the fingers. Lift clear vertically, then start moving the camera toward white and the watch toward red with grippers held closed.
Carry the retained camera and watch fully over their separate baskets, then lower slightly while maintaining the grasps.
Release the camera into white and watch into red, clear the rims, and begin approaching the remaining camera and green watch.
Approach the front camera with left and green watch with right, retaining separate workspaces and stopping above grasp height for visual correction.
Lower to the camera and green watch with small back-and-side corrections, then close gently at the estimated object heights.
Test retention with a vertical lift of the last camera and green watch, then start toward the assigned baskets while keeping both grippers closed.
The last camera is retained; carry it to white. The green watch remained on the table, so reopen right and reapproach lower at its shifted position.
The camera slipped onto the table during transit; return above its new location. Regrasp the green watch lower and slightly right, then test lift.
Descend left over the recovered camera. The green watch now appears pinched securely; lift vertically and verify before transporting farther.
Pinch the recovered camera near its middle and test-lift; transport the visibly retained green watch toward the red basket without changing orientation.
Lift and slowly transport the more central camera grasp to white. Lower and release the green watch inside red, then lift clear.
Finish positioning the retained camera over white. Move the open right gripper toward the last watch near the center, staying on the right side.
Release the last camera into white and withdraw toward the cyan vehicle. Right approaches the remaining watch from above, without crossing the midline.
Approach the cyan vehicle with left. Lower right into the last watch's band and close, using the earlier successful watch height as a guide.
Center and close left on the taxi, then test lift. Raise the last watch vertically to verify retention before carrying to red.
Taxi was not retained; reopen and approach its middle lower. Carry the visibly retained final watch to red with a smooth constant-orientation path.
Close lower around the taxi body and test retention. The final watch slipped during transit; return right to regrasp it more centrally.
Taxi appears securely retained; lift before moving toward blue. Right descends toward the watch housing for a deeper, more central grasp.
Carry the taxi smoothly toward blue. Lower right to the watch housing, close, and test-lift while keeping the right EE on its side of the centerline.
Position taxi over blue. The watch is hooked off-center rather than securely pinched; reopen and grasp deeper around its band with a slight leftward correction.
Replan after the rejected suffix: release taxi from the current safe position over blue, then retract. Lift the regrasped watch vertically to verify retention.
The watch housing appears retained; carry slowly toward red. Once right clears the center, bring left above the remaining gold vehicle.
Lower the left gripper over the gold vehicle while carrying the retained final watch completely over the red basket.
Advance left to pinch the middle of the gold vehicle. Lower and release the last watch into red, then raise the open right gripper.
Lift the gold vehicle with the left grip closed to verify retention. All three watches are visible in red; retract the open right arm toward its origin.
The gold vehicle slipped; reopen and change to a steeper top-down approach over its body. Finish the right arm's gradual return toward origin.
Replan after the right-arm continuity rejection with much smaller return increments. Lower the open left gripper under its steeper approach and refine gold-vehicle alignment.
Descend around the gold vehicle's sides under the steeper approach, close, and make a short test lift. Right remains open near origin.
The gold vehicle is hanging between the fingers. Lift it clear of the blue rim and begin a slow short carry, keeping the grasp closed and orientation fixed.
Move the retained vehicle just inside blue with small forward increments and a gentle wrist tilt, maintaining rim clearance and configuration continuity.
After the IK interruption, release from the current position over blue rather than advancing farther. Retract slowly away from the reach boundary, with both grippers open.
Both vehicles are now inside blue. Replan the rejected retreat using millimeter-scale increments to leave the near-singular configuration continuously before returning home.
The previous retreat changed elbow geometry unexpectedly. Reverse that small motion slowly to recover the earlier configuration before attempting a different return path.
Retrace the earlier approach away from the basket to recover more elbow-up reach margin. Both grippers remain open; sorted objects remain undisturbed.
The elbow geometry did not recover as expected. Reverse this short segment cautiously, then reassess before further retreat; leave all basket contents untouched.
Use submillimeter corrections toward the last known configuration before the branch change, keeping both grippers open and monitoring continuity closely.
Try a very small inward-and-lower retreat with orientation fixed, checking that elbow-up continuity recovers rather than moving farther toward extension.
Undo the small retreat that worsened elbow geometry; recover the previous pose before selecting a different wrist-and-arm return path.
Change wrist pitch very slightly while easing backward, seeking the continuous elbow-up return path without disturbing the sorted baskets.
Continue the small pitch-and-backward correction that reduced the elbow angle, monitoring continuity before a larger return motion.
Probe a millimeter-scale vertical correction with fixed orientation to determine the safe continuous direction away from the elbow singularity.
Retrace the earlier steeper wrist approach in small increments while easing back from the basket, aiming to recover the elbow-up return configuration.
Use a tiny upward-and-backward arc instead of further straight retreat, seeking a continuous elbow-up escape from the reach boundary.
Elbow angle has recovered on the desired side. Retract left toward home with increasing reach margin and gradually level the wrist; make a tiny right-origin correction.
The rejected call moved neither arm. Restart the same inward retreat with substantially smaller initial increments to keep elbow changes below the continuity guard.
Continue the now-clear elbow-up retreat toward origin, gradually leveling the left wrist while leaving all sorted objects untouched.
Return the left arm close to its original pose with a smooth, open-gripper descent and wrist leveling; keep right at origin.
